abstract: This paper studies Distribution Regression (DR) for ordered and discrete outcomes that are only partially observed due to misreporting. Such outcomes frequently occur in self‐reported surveys eliciting socially undesirable, illegal or stigmatised behaviours like substance abuse, domestic violence or anti‐social behaviour. We demonstrate that DR can offer a flexible way to study the distribution of these outcomes. Specifically, we analyse the asymptotic properties of the DR estimator and derive simultaneous confidence bands for unconditional ‘survival’ probabilities generated by that estimator as well as for counterfactual functionals thereof. The method is illustrated by examining possibly underreported lifetime marijuana consumption behaviour among US high‐school students. We find significant, positive differences across some consumption frequencies in lifetime marijuana use between students residing in states with and without recreational marijuana laws.
journal: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics
title: Distribution Regression for Partially Observed Discrete, Ordered Outcomes—The Case of Adolescent Substance Abuse
title_zh: 部分观测离散有序结果的分布回归——青少年药物滥用案例

abstract: This paper relies on a novel dataset of more than 31,000 industrial policies in around 150 economies over the period 2009–2022 to codify and examine the stated objectives and design characteristics of these policies. Using large‐scale machine learning methods applied to policy texts, we systematically classify policy objectives at a global level and document several new stylised facts. We find that industrial policies increasingly pursue multiple objectives, often ones that may be hard to reconcile. In a two‐way fixed effects framework, we show that industrial policies with environmental objectives are more common in Western economies while secure supply objectives are more common in economies geopolitically aligned with China. The majority of industrial policies exhibit features that may make them prone to capture by special interests: they discriminate against foreigners, are firm‐specific and lack ‘sunset clauses’. Industrial policies which reduce firms' costs (such as subsidies, as opposed to taxes) have become more common over time, in particular in rival geopolitical blocs. These features of industrial policies highlight the importance and challenges of evaluating their value‐for‐money, which, in turn, requires clear identification of the primary objective of each policy.

title: Moving the Goalposts: The Changing Objectives of Industrial Policy

abstract: Seeds are the ‘chips’ of agriculture; the use and promotion of improved seeds are crucial for ensuring food security. This study employs Rehmannia glutinosa as a case study and conducts a joint measurement experiment on farmers' risk and time preferences in rural China. This study aimed to assess the contribution of cognitive ability to farmers' adoption of agricultural technology and to identify potential underlying channels. The study builds upon and extends prior research on the determinants of farmers' adoption of agricultural technologies. The results indicate that higher cognitive ability increases the likelihood of adopting improved seed technology. Farmers with greater cognitive ability exhibit lower risk aversion and greater patience, making them more likely to adopt such innovations. Overall, this study has substantial practical implications for advancing the dissemination of improved agricultural seeds.

abstract: Growth in household debt‐to‐income ratios reflects nominal debt changes or “Fisher dynamics” due to interest income and expenses, real income growth, and inflation. Using two decades of microdata on all Norwegian households, we decompose these channels' roles in how debt‐to‐income evolves over time and in response to monetary policy shocks. On average, debt changes outsize Fisher dynamics, except among highly leveraged households. After interest rate hikes, the channels pull in opposite directions, but the debt changes dominate, so debt‐to‐income ratios decline. This holds across subgroups, including highly indebted households, recent movers, and those facing liquidity constraints or high unemployment risk.
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title: Fisher Dynamics, Monetary Policy, and Household Indebtedness
title_zh: 费雪动态、货币政策与家庭债务

abstract: Do financial constraints determine the transmission of monetary policy? I examine this question using the staggered enactment of anti-recharacterization legislation as a source of exogenous variation in creditor rights that loosens firm-financial constraints. A 25 basis-point expansionary monetary policy shock results in a 2 percentage-point higher investment growth among treated (unconstrained) firms. This reflects their flatter marginal cost curves for financing, which amplifies responses to shifts in the marginal benefit curve. The relationship, however, reverses during economic downturns when investment opportunities are scarce. I rationalize these findings in a static model and quantify the channels using a Heterogeneous Agent New Keynesian model.
title: Financial constraints and the transmission of monetary policy: Evidence from relaxation of collateral constraints
title_zh: 融资约束与货币政策传导：来自抵押约束放松的证据

abstract: The productivity of Artificial Intelligence in education depends critically on technology adoption and user effort. We estimate the causal effect of AI design on student learning, comparing a “curriculum-tailored” chatbot to a “general-purpose” model. In a large-scale randomized controlled trial with 2440 students, we find the primary barrier to AI’s effectiveness is student engagement. The tailored chatbot increases task completion by 13.2 percentage points, while the generic tool has no effect relative to traditional instruction. This increase in engagement translates into learning gains. Conservative Intent-to-Treat estimates show the tailored tool increases immediate human capital accumulation by 0.126 standard deviations. For compliers—students induced to participate by the tailored design—the effects are large and durable, with module completion increasing long-term knowledge retention by 0.309 standard deviations. These findings demonstrate that the returns to educational AI depend fundamentally on design choices that overcome behavioral constraints to participation.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
source_issue: Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization, Volume 252
title: The tailoring premium: AI design, behavioral engagement, and human capital formation
title_zh: 定制溢价：人工智能设计、行为参与与人力资本形成

abstract: We conduct a survey experiment with a politically representative sample of more than 5,000 U.S. consumers to study how perceptions of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) political stance shape macroeconomic expectations, trust, and information processing. Overall, 63.5% of respondents view the Fed as politically neutral, 9.4% as aligned with their own party (in-group), and 27.2% as opposed (out-group). The non-neutral minority differs sharply: out-group respondents report substantially higher inflation expectations and lower trust than neutral or in-group respondents, even after controlling for partisanship and demographics. They also pay more to avoid opposing media and are less likely to receive Fed communication—yet update their expectations by more once exposed to it, placing less weight on their priors when the same article carries a Fed label. In a hypothetical Trump presidency, the neutral share falls to 37.2%, with respondents in both parties shifting toward viewing the Fed as Republican-leaning, consistent with expected political capture. Perceived neutrality is thus central to the Fed’s credibility and the reach of its communication, and it can shift with changes in political leadership.
journal: Journal of the European Economic Association
title: Perceived Political Bias of the Federal Reserve,
title_zh: 美联储被感知的政治偏见

abstract: Despite stagnant economic and living conditions, early 20th-century colonial Jamaica experienced a remarkable increase in life expectancy, a phenomenon referred to as the Jamaica Paradox. One factor believed to be key in this transformation was the Hookworm Campaign (1919–1936), an island-wide, multi-faceted public health initiative to eradicate hookworm that not only involved de-worming treatments but also improved sanitation and the provision of health education. Using parish-level mortality data and a staggered DID framework, we investigate whether the campaign reduced mortality rates in Jamaica. Results show that deaths among infants, very young children, and the elderly declined by around 20, within ten years of programme implementation, but other age groups were not affected. Our estimates suggest that by WWII the hookworm eradication effort increased life expectancy at birth by 3 years, accounting for 43 per cent of its observed rise during this period. A ‘back-of-the-envelope’ cost–benefit analysis reveals that the benefits in terms of spared deaths were multiple times the campaign costs, but that the local population likely shouldered most of the overall costs.
title: The Jamaica life expectancy paradox: The role of the hookworm campaign
title_zh: 牙买加预期寿命悖论：钩虫运动的作用

abstract: We provide simple and easily verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions for infinite-horizon continuous-time optimal control problems. Under standard concavity and integrability assumptions, we show that optimal paths are fully characterized by first-order conditions together with a transversality condition. Importantly, the transversality condition is derived as a consequence of the model’s structure rather than imposed a priori. Our results apply directly to standard economic models, including optimal growth and consumption–saving problems.
title: A note on first-order and transversality conditions in infinite-horizon continuous-time optimal control models
title_zh: 无限期连续时间最优控制模型中一阶条件与横截性条件的注记

abstract: Phase III of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) replaced free allocation with auctioning as the default method of distributing allowances in the power sector. Auctioning has generally been regarded as providing stronger incentives for renewable deployment, yet this policy proposition has rarely been tested directly. Article 10c created a unique institutional setting in which some lower-income Member States could retain free allocation, conditional on reinvesting the equivalent allowance value in renewable energy and power sector modernization. We exploit this institutional variation to test whether auctioning generated stronger renewable deployment than conditional free allocation. We combine a partial equilibrium model with an empirical analysis of EU ETS data. The theoretical model shows that under full carbon cost pass-through, auctioning does not increase carbon costs borne by power generators, while free allocation generates windfall profits. In either case, renewables gain no relative cost advantage over fossil fuels, implying that the allocation method alone does not change firms' incentives to deploy renewable capacity. Consistent with this prediction, our difference-in-differences estimates show that renewable capacity expanded and power sector emissions declined during Phase III, yet we find no statistically significant evidence that auctioning generated stronger renewable deployment or greater emissions reductions than conditional free allocation. As more countries adopt emissions trading systems, our findings suggest that, within the institutional setting examined here, their effectiveness in promoting renewable deployment may depend less on the allocation method itself than on enforceable governance mechanisms that channel allowance value toward low-carbon investment.
title: To auction or to give for free: Does the allowance allocation regime matter for renewable deployment in the EU ETS?
title_zh: 拍卖还是免费分配：欧盟排放交易体系中配额分配机制对可再生能源部署是否重要？

abstract: The world’s top destination country for migrant workers, the United States, is enacting a set of unprecedented taxes on high-skill immigration that include charging employers roughly $100,000 for each foreign worker they hire using the H-1B visa. The US government has relied on one academic study to design the tax and evaluate its impact on high-skill immigration under the H-1B quota, an impact the study estimates at zero by measuring the wage di!erences between H-1B and native workers. This paper precisely replicates the study’s method and ”nds that its conclusion rests on three major flaws, each of which renders its results difficult to interpret. The study mismeasures the wage gap between H-1B and native workers, misinterprets any negative wage gap as reflecting markdowns rather than task specialization, and carries the wage results into a policy simulation whose central estimates are invariant to the wage gap: they predict an identical (null) e!ect on immigration for any H-1B wage gap including zero. Improved methods are required to o!er regulators useful information on the e!ects of this large shift in immigration policy.
title: Taxing high-skill immigration: Fundamental problems in evaluating immigrant-native wage gaps and the H-1B visa tax
title_zh: 对高技能移民征税：评估移民与本土工资差距及H-1B签证税的根本问题

abstract: We study whether firms in medium-scale New Keynesian models would voluntarily satisfy demand at their posted prices, or whether nominal rigidities may push prices below marginal costs. In the Altig et al. (2011) framework, which features full indexation of non-adjusting prices and wages to steady-state inflation and near constant returns to scale at the firm level, we find that violations of firms’ willingness-to-supply condition are negligible: fewer than one percent of firms are ever constrained, and the associated output losses are tiny. Two features of the model drive this result: marginal costs that are nearly unresponsive to output, and prices that adjust more frequently than wages. When the short-run marginal-cost schedule is sufficiently steep, willingness-to-supply violations become quantitatively relevant. Our findings thus characterize the conditions under which the standard demand-determination assumption is a reliable approximation and those under which it may not be.
journal: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control

abstract: We develop a non-stochastic version of Miao and Wang (2018) that preserves its key equilibrium mechanisms while allowing explicit computation of the fundamental value. We show that the stock price equals its fundamental value and that the price-to-dividend ratio remains constant over time. Hence, the stock price does not constitute a rational bubble in the standard theoretical sense. Our results support the critique of Hirano and Toda (2025). At the same time, our analysis suggests that the framework of Miao and Wang (2018) offers a useful alternative perspective on asset price dynamics alongside the standard rational bubble theory. We further clarify the distinction between equilibrium multiplicity and rational bubbles and contribute to a systematic classification of bubble theories.
title: On rational bubbles with dividends: A note on
title_zh: 论带股利的理性泡沫：一则注记

abstract: We study tie-breaking favoritism in a costly voting model with a common fixed voting cost and Poisson population uncertainty. One candidate wins a tied election with probability greater than 1 / 2 . Although this rule directly favors that candidate, it also induces an opposing strategic turnout response. At every interior equilibrium, the favored candidate receives fewer votes in expectation and, more surprisingly, wins the election with probability below 1 / 2 . The strategic effect more than offsets the direct effect for any degree of favoritism. Thus, any asymmetric tie-breaking rule disadvantages the candidate it favors.
title: The electoral disadvantage of a tie-breaking advantage
title_zh: 打破平局优势的选举劣势

abstract: In a lab experiment, groups in ring or complete networks estimate a common parameter using a common signal, private signals, and the past guesses of group members. Although the informational content is identical, the order in which signals arrive has a strong effect on the groups’ final beliefs. I identify the main mechanism behind this effect: participants place a fixed weight on their private signal regardless of when it arrives, whereas Bayesian updating requires this weight to fall as information accumulates; signals that arrive later are consequently overrepresented in final beliefs. The effect is social in origin: in an individual-level experiment with the same information structure and no network, participants make correct adjustments. A denser network and, especially, sequential rather than simultaneous information release both substantially reduce correlation neglect.
title: An Experiment on Social Learning with Information Sequencing
title_zh: 信息序列下的社会学习实验

abstract: In recent years, there has been considerable interest in understanding the climate–migration relationship. While most studies concern the rural populations, little is known about the relationship between climate change and high-skilled workers. In this paper, we construct a panel data set of inventors on annual bilateral migration flows in China to investigate the relationship between climate-related disasters and inventor mobility. We find that inventor mobility is sensitive to climate-related disasters. Climate-related disasters in origin cities drive inventors to leave, while climate-related disasters in destination cities suppress the inflow of inventors, especially in cities with weaker economic development. Inventors who possess a high capacity for innovation are more prone to being affected by climate-related disasters. Moreover, climate-related disasters also affect inventors’ choices of cities in which they undertake their initial employment. The inflow of inventors has a positive effect on the number of urban innovations, and this effect is stronger in less developed cities. Inventor outflows reduce innovation in less developed cities, while such detrimental effects are not present in more developed cities.

abstract: As climate-related disasters become more frequent and intense, understanding how herders respond to drought risk is critical for strengthening resilience in pastoral areas. Existing studies have widely examined the determinants of adaptive behaviours. However, they have paid limited attention to prior disaster experience, which may shape decision-making through learning, memory, and risk perception. This study employed a bivariate probit model to quantify the association between drought experience and adaptive behaviours and examine the potential mechanisms using survey data from 519 herder households across six counties in Inner Mongolia, China. The results show that prior drought exposure is positively associated with herders’ adaptive responses, particularly preventive adaptation. Drought-induced economic losses are also positively associated with adaptation, whereas longer time since the most severe drought is associated with a lower probability of adjustment-oriented responses. Moreover, some of these associations are more pronounced among female herders and, separately, among herders in ecologically fragile grassland areas. We also found that herders’ perception of drought severity partially mediates the association between drought experience and preventive adaptation. These findings call for better access to meteorological disaster and adaptation information, stronger drought risk perception among herders, and greater participation of female herders in disaster preparedness.

title: Learning from drought: does prior experience enhance herders’ adaptive responses?

abstract: We study the impact of digital finance on the green development level of the economy using data from 30 provinces of China from 2011 to 2021. The main findings are as follows: (1) Digital finance significantly enhances the level of regional economic green development, and this conclusion remains valid after a series of robustness tests. (2) The impact of digital finance on economic green development exhibits a threshold effect. Specifically, the green-promoting effect strengthens considerably once the threshold variable surpasses a critical value. (3) Mechanism analysis indicates that digital finance facilitates economic green development through two channels: incentivizing green technology innovation and enhancing the innovation value realization. (4) Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the green-promoting effect is more pronounced in regions with greater usage depth of digital finance, higher levels of digitization, eastern location, and more advanced digital infrastructure. (5) Spatial econometric results confirm spatial dependence in economic green development and a statistically significant direct effect of digital finance on regional green development.

title: Digital finance and economic green development

abstract: Tax incentives not only reduce corporate tax burdens and encourage investment, but also serve as favourable signals to investors, potentially enhancing firms’ attractiveness to patient capital (PC). Using a sample of Chinese listed firms from 2007 to 2024, we examine the effects of two tax incentives: corporate income tax preferences and the pretax additional deduction for R&D expenditure (PADRDE), on firms’ PC. The results indicate that: (1) both corporate income tax preferences and PADRDE stimulate corporate PC, measured by PC ownership stability index; (2) mechanism tests suggest that alleviated financing constraints, increased innovation investment, and promoted financial transparency partially mediate the relationship between tax incentives and corporate PC; and (3) heterogeneity analyses show stronger associations between income tax preferences and corporate PC for non-SOEs, whereas the association between PADRDE and corporate PC is stronger for firms in less marketized regions and those with lower R&D intensity. Overall, the results suggest that corporate tax relief can simultaneously support supply-side upgrading and expansionary demand management. For capital market participants, corporate tax benefits may also signal stronger long-term growth prospects. During technological transitions, tax relief targeted at technologically advanced firms can help mobilize social capital for innovation and facilitate industrial upgrading.

title: Impact of tax incentives on corporate patient capital: evidence from income tax preferences and pretax additional deduction on R&D expenditure in China

abstract: This article examines how the market roles of Bitcoin and gold evolved over the 2020–2026 period of institutional maturity. Departing from static linear correlations, we combine a time–frequency framework – bivariate, partial, and multiple wavelet coherence – with multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis and asymmetric-risk metrics (the Omega and a Sharpe ratio). Partial and multiple estimators isolate the intrinsic equity linkage of each asset from the surrounding monetary environment, mapping the distinct channels through which systemic shocks are transmitted. The evidence is consistent with a pro-cyclical, high-beta profile for Bitcoin: its co-movement with equities persists once real interest rates and central bank liquidity are partialled out, and its anti-phase relationship with market fear implies participation in sell-offs. The decisive distinction from gold is directional rather than one of magnitude. Microstructurally the two assets are comparably efficient in normal conditions and comparably fragile in the tails; they differ in the composition of their macro-financial dependence – gold organized around the currency and rate complex, Bitcoin around equities and volatility. Their risk-adjusted profiles are mirror-images across horizons: gold a dependable short-horizon stabilizer, Bitcoin a diversifier whose return asymmetry translates into long-term growth only over extended holding periods.
title: Safe-Haven dynamics and financialization: a multiscale wavelet and asymmetric risk analysis of Bitcoin and gold
title_zh: 避险资产动态与金融化：比特币与黄金的多尺度小波与非对称风险分析

abstract: We use Canadian matched employer-employee data to assess the sources of the union pay premium. After controlling for worker heterogeneity using the two-way fixed effects approach of Abowd, Kramarz, and Margolis (AKM), we find that unionized firms pay about 15 log points more than non-unionized firms. Forty percent of this gap is linked to productivity differences between unionized and non-unionized firms as measured by value added per worker. The remaining gap reflects unions’ ability to extract more rents for workers. Our estimates imply that unions raise pay among unionized workers by around 9 log points, with considerable heterogeneity by industry and firm birth cohorts. The union effect grows to about 11 log points in an extension of the AKM approach where unions also affect the returns to unobservable worker characteristics.
title: Why Do Union Jobs Pay More? New Evidence from Matched Employer-Employee Data
title_zh: 工会工作为何薪酬更高？来自匹配雇主-雇员数据的新证据

abstract: Energy poverty remains a major concern in less-developed nations where mineral-dependent economies are increasingly exposed to fluctuations in international critical mineral prices (CMP). This research examines the impact of CMP on access to energy, in 95 developing countries over 1990-2023 by employing panel time fixed effects, Lewbel-type instrumental variables, system-GMM, and local projection methods. The findings reveal that an increase in CMP significantly improves access to clean cooking fuels and technologies. Further, results are not sensitive to changes in estimation method, but region-wise differences are observed, indicating that economic and institutional factors across nations have different impacts on their renewable energy policies. The mediation analysis shows that mineral rents and investment channels provide partial mediation, whereas the financial development channel helps transmit mineral-specific gains to energy access. In addition, the dynamic local projections show distinct transmission responses of energy access to CMP shocks. The findings extend resource-based development perspectives by showing that the energy-access implications of CMP movements depend not only on price changes but also on how these gains are transmitted through economic and financial channels and conditioned by institutional quality.
title: Do international critical mineral prices influence energy access? Evidence from developing countries
title_zh: 国际关键矿产价格是否影响能源获取？来自发展中国家的证据

abstract: Türkiye is approaching the commissioning of its first commercial nuclear power plant, yet almost no quantitative evidence exists on how its public views radioactive waste management. This study reports an online survey of 497 respondents conducted in October–December 2025, measuring objective knowledge of radioactive waste, perceived risk, trust in the responsible organizations, and acceptance. Objective knowledge was low: respondents answered a mean of 2.33 of five factual items correctly, and 12.9% knew that properly contained waste does not continuously emit radiation. Perceived risk was uniformly high (M = 4.29 on a five-point scale), greatest on consequences for future generations and on accidents during nuclear waste transport. Trust was uneven: government statements (M = 2.56) and media reporting (M = 2.32) fell below the midpoint of the scale, while scientific explanations (M = 3.58), international inspections (M = 3.42), and the competence of Turkish engineers (M = 3.28) lay above it. Acceptance was low (M = 2.69), and 76.1% rejected a waste facility near their own city. Knowledge was unrelated to perceived risk (r = −0.078, p > 0.05) and to acceptance (r = 0.007, p > 0.05), and weakly related to trust (r = 0.186, p < 0.001), whereas perceived risk was strongly associated with trust (r = −0.583, p < 0.001) and trust with acceptance (r = 0.513, p < 0.001). Communication addressing only factual knowledge is therefore unlikely to change how this risk is perceived. The results provide a baseline recorded before commercial operation begins.
title: Quantitative analysis of public perception regarding nuclear waste in Türkiye: Knowledge level, risk perception, and trust indicators
title_zh: 土耳其公众对核废料认知的定量分析：知识水平、风险感知与信任指标

abstract: This paper examines how firms’ exposure to physical climate risk affects innovative human capital. Inventors are more likely to leave as their employers become more exposed to climate shocks. Inventors departing firms with rising exposure tend to join less-exposed employers. The departure response reflects employer-level exposure rather than shocks confined to inventors’ own locations. Consistent with a career-concern channel, greater climate exposure predicts persistently slower R&D growth, and departing inventors sort toward firms with stronger innovative environments. The resulting reallocation is economically consequential: more exposed firms lose highly productive and valuable inventors, and inventor departures are followed by deterioration in subsequent innovation outcomes.
title: Climate exposure and the flight of inventors
title_zh: 气候暴露与发明家外流

abstract: Over the past decade, hedge funds have increasingly embraced green investing. We develop a novel return-based measure of fund greenness and find that greener funds earn higher average returns, consistent with capturing a positive green premium, and are associated with lower risks, especially during adverse periods. We further show that performance gains are greatest among directional funds, whereas risk reduction is most pronounced among nondirectional funds. We also provide evidence that managers of these funds exhibit superior green investment skills through green stock selection and green factor timing. Finally, investors reward greener hedge funds only when they demonstrate strong performance.
journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
title: Are the Hedges of Funds Green?
title_zh: 基金的绿色对冲有效吗？

abstract: This paper examines whether the association between e-government maturity and shadow economy size depends on the level of telecommunications infrastructure. We develop a theoretical account in which connectivity does two things at once: it extends access to public digital services, and it expands private digital markets that absorb part of the cost-sensitive informal population. Because both act on the same finite population, the marginal formalisation return to e-government maturity should diminish as connectivity rises. Using 10 waves of the UN E-Government Survey covering 105 countries between 2003 and 2020, a two-way fixed-effects specification yields the positive and significant interaction this implies. Further, the interaction is stronger where the informal sector is structurally larger, measured by agricultural employment, and the attenuation reproduces on the European Commission VAT compliance gap, an administrative outcome independent of the model-based series. For policymakers, the association between e-government maturity and informality is strongest where connectivity is limited and the informal sector is large, and it weakens as connectivity rises. Where connectivity is already high, improvements in e-government maturity are unlikely to register in shadow economy statistics. Identification rests on cross-national rather than within-country variation, so the results are reported as conditional associations rather than causal effects.
title: Connectivity matters: the conditional association between E-Government maturity and shadow economy size
title_zh: 连通性至关重要：电子政务成熟度与影子经济规模之间的条件关联

abstract: In Afghanistan, land ownership has long shifted with political power. Successive regime changes have reshaped who is recognised as an owner, who can occupy property, and how territorial resources are redistributed. The Taliban’s return in 2021 did not produce formal land reform, but it reopened a familiar pattern in which political transition unsettles property relations and enables new forms of control. Drawing on qualitative interviews with Afghan landowners now living in exile, this article examines how ownership moves between informal occupation and formal recognition. Houses, plots, and commercial spaces often remain legally tied to former owners while authority is renegotiated on the ground. In some cases, occupation becomes institutionalised through administrative approval, new documentation, or policy measures that regularise access for politically aligned actors. Property change therefore unfolds less as a single act of confiscation than as a layered process through which possession, mediation, and emerging governance practices redefine ownership. The analysis shows how struggles over land operate as a mechanism for reassembling political order. Ownership becomes increasingly difficult to exercise across distance, producing conditions in which property may persist on paper or be reassigned through governmental decree, while recognition and effective control shift in practice. By foregrounding absent owners and unsettled claims, the article contributes to land use policy debates on restitution, return, and post-conflict land administration, with implications for other fragile political environments.
title: Who owns the land after regime collapse? Shifting land claims and tenure governance in post-2021 Afghanistan
title_zh: 2021年后阿富汗政权崩溃后的土地归属：土地权利主张与权属治理的变迁

abstract: This study examines the impacts of GVC participation and its components on financial development across 55 economies from 2000 to 2018. Grounded in the openness theory of financial development, we employ panel fixed effects, panel quantile regression and dynamic panel threshold regression to analyse how GVC integration through trade openness, financial openness, and demand for financial services influences financial development. Our results show that GVC participation has a positive and significant influence on financial development regardless of a country's existing financial market development, though the effect diminishes at higher quantiles. The dynamic panel threshold regression reveals a clear dichotomy: GVC participation is positively associated with financial development in lower growth economies but negatively associated with it in higher‐growth economies. We verify the robustness of this dichotomy by classifying economies as advanced or emerging using the IMF World Economic Outlook classification. The bootstrap bias‐corrected fixed‐effects results, estimated separately for each income group, corroborate the divergent effects documented in the main analysis. Additionally, we employ domestic credit to the private sector, the Financial Markets Index, and the Financial Institutions Index as alternative proxies for financial development, all of which confirm the baseline findings. Our results underscore the need for tailored GVC strategies across different stages of economic development.
title:
Unravelling the
                    GVC
                    ‐Finance Nexus: Divergent Effects in Developed and Developing Economies

abstract: We document how foreign firms and inputs have shaped the development of Viet Nam's solar panel industry. We use firm‐to‐firm transaction data from Panjiva as well as firm‐level data from the Vietnamese Enterprise Survey to trace solar panel value chains. We uncover three key findings: First, China provides the majority of solar inputs to Vietnamese producers, and these are 50% cheaper than those from other countries on average. Second, Chinese FDI firms dominate Viet Nam's solar industry, accounting for 75% of exports and 50% of jobs, and they export solar panels that are 54% cheaper than those of other producers in Viet Nam. Third, local firms supplying parts and components to these Chinese FDI firms experience positive productivity gains. Our findings show how Viet Nam's solar boom emerged through deep integration into China's supply chains.

abstract: As an important practice of multifunctional peri-urban ecological governance under the Park City strategy, the Chengdu peri-urban ecological zone (CDPUEZ) integrates cropland protection, urban growth control, ecological restoration, and public green space development within a unified governance framework, providing a representative case for examining the transition from traditional boundary-based greenbelts to multifunctional nature-based solutions (NbS) in rapidly urbanizing megacities. This study evaluated the effects of CDPUEZ construction on agricultural-urban-ecological spaces and identified its policy effects. By combining counterfactual simulation, spatial gradient analysis, and quasi-experimental causal inference, we evaluated the spatiotemporal evolution of cropland fragmentation, urban expansion, and habitat quality during 2016–2024 within an integrated evaluation framework. The results indicated that (1) following policy implementation (2020–2024), cropland fragmentation within the CDPUEZ increased by 0.94%, considerably lower than the 14.80% surge projected under the no-policy counterfactual scenario, indicating that the policy effectively mitigated potential fragmentation growth. (2) Compared with the counterfactual scenario, urban expansion rate within the CDPUEZ decreased from 11.40% to 3.49%, while the dominant expansion type shifted from edge-expansion to infilling. (3) Habitat quality within the CDPUEZ declined by approximately 1.61%, lower than the 5.65% projected under the counterfactual scenario, indicating that the CDPUEZ contributed to mitigating habitat degradation. (4) Causal analyses showed significant positive policy effects across different spatial gradient reference ranges, further proving the robustness of the findings. However, peripheral areas continued to experience relatively high cropland fragmentation and urban development pressure, indicating a spatially uneven distribution of policy benefits. Future ecological planning should strengthen cross-boundary governance to address persistent peripheral pressures, while the proposed multidimensional framework provides a potential approach for evaluating large-scale ecological infrastructure and NbS globally.

abstract: This paper examines the comparative advantages of shadow banks across market segments. Combining credit bureau data on retail loans in India with weather shocks as a proxy for credit demand, we show that Fintechs respond more in uncollateralized markets. In contrast, non-Fintech shadow banks exhibit stronger responsiveness in collateralized markets. Exploiting geographic heterogeneity in the adoption of digital payments, we identify technology as the key advantage for Fintechs. Leveraging four natural experiments, we document the significance of lower regulation for non-Fintech shadow banks. Our results suggest that the comparative advantage of shadow banks differs across market segments.
title: Shadow banks on the rise: Evidence across market segments
title_zh: 影子银行的崛起：来自各市场细分的证据

abstract: Politicians have long pressed central banks for lower interest rates in the belief that easy money wins elections. This column tests that premise using 385 parliamentary and presidential elections in 18 countries between 1900 and 2020. It finds no evidence that easy money helps incumbents. The most likely electoral return to a typical easing is close to zero, and large returns are ruled out. A modest return can be decisive only in exceptionally close races. The electoral case for pressing central banks is weak.
authors: Yao Chen, Felix Ward, Florian van Genderen
title: Easy money does not win elections
title_zh: 宽松货币赢不了选举

abstract: High public debt around the globe has revived concerns that it could undo central banks’ ability to control inflation. Higher debt can lead to higher spending and increase inflation if households do not fully save debt-financed transfers. This column argues that central banks can still control inflation in these situations, but they must act following increases in debt levels and before they translate into higher inflation. Crucially, central banks should take into account that higher public debt increases the level of interest rates consistent with price stability.
title: Monetary policy in times of high public debt
title_zh: 高公共债务时期的货币政策

abstract: The 2024 revision of China's Company Law formally codifies the pre-establishment national treatment and negative list systems piloted in free trade zones (FTZs), marking a transition to rule-based institutional opening-up. Amidst rising geopolitical fragmentation, a critical question arises: Can such institutional certainty effectively anchor foreign capital? This paper exploits the staggered rollout of FTZs (2013−2022) as a quasi-natural experiment to provide causal evidence on the economic consequences of these now-universalized reforms. Using comprehensive firm-level registration data and robust staggered difference-in-differences estimators, we document a striking asymmetric expansion in FDI. We document an asymmetric expansionary effect driven by institutional opening-up, significantly expanding the extensive margin of wholly foreign-owned enterprises (WFOEs) alongside a stable formation of joint ventures (JVs). Crucially, we find this effect is resilient to fluctuations in geopolitical risk, suggesting that institutional certainty acts as a safe harbor for investment. Mechanism analyses reveal the effect is driven by comprehensive institutional reforms rather than selective industrial policies, favoring R&D-intensive and trade-oriented entrants. These findings provide the empirical basis for the implementation of the 2024 Company Law.

abstract: Belief-dependent preferences capture psychological motivations such as emotions and image concerns. To manage certain emotions, some agents may prefer not to premeditate their behavior, but to remain undecided and act spontaneously. This raises conceptual and analytical challenges. We show that a rational agent never needs to act spontaneously if, at every history, his decision utility does not depend on what he planned to do at past or counterfactual histories. Decision problems with anticipatory emotions are a common class of psychological games where this property holds. To illustrate, we study the effects of savoring and dread on intertemporal choice. We find that behavior with and without commitment only coincides if the agent’s emotions are very mild or very intense. Dynamic inconsistency arises for an intermediate range of emotional intensity.
title: Rational Planning and Self Consistency in Decision Problems with Anticipatory Emotions
title_zh: 预期情绪下决策问题中的理性规划与自我一致性

abstract: Equilibria of cheap-talk games in which the sender has state-independent preferences are generally not robust to introducing slight dependence on the state. Some equilibria, however, can be approximated by robust equilibria of nearby cheap-talk games with slightly state-dependent sender preferences. We characterize these equilibria for all games with binary state space and show that, in particular, the maximal equilibrium payoff for the sender can always be robustly approximated in this sense.
title: Robust equilibria in cheap-talk games with fairly transparent motives
title_zh: 在动机相当透明的廉价谈话博弈中的稳健均衡

abstract: We conduct a randomized controlled trial of a micro-hydro electrification project in a rural community in Kenya with staggered household connections beginning in 2016, allowing us to study effects up to eight years after connection. We find that electricity access affects economic activity, but only in the long run. Households increase time spent on non-farm work by 78 percent and reduce time on farm work, consistent with the early stages of structural transformation, yet these effects emerge only after four years. Electrification leads to business creation and expansion, higher profits, greater employment, and increased use of electricity in production. Adoption of electrical appliances follows a clear temporal pattern: lights and mobile phones are adopted immediately; smartphones with internet access spread gradually; and computers are adopted only after eight years, particularly among households with positive savings. These results highlight that measuring the returns to rural electrification requires a long time horizon to capture its full economic effects.
title: The long-run returns to rural electrification: Evidence from a randomized experiment
title_zh: 农村电气化的长期回报：来自随机实验的证据

abstract: Sound economic policy formulation requires high frequency economic activity data. This is particularly challenging in low-income, fragile, and conflict-affected states, such as Afghanistan, where quarterly GDP data is unavailable and annual GDP figures are published with considerable delays. This paper utilizes an innovative approach for estimating quarterly economic activity under these constraints, facilitating timely economic assessments in Afghanistan. Quarterly GDP data are interpolated from annual figures, utilizing money supply as a proxy indicator of economic activities due to Afghanistan’s predominately cash-based economy. By leveraging machine learning, traditional (macroeconomic), non-traditional (satellite) data, the approach provides real-time insights of the underlying direction of the Afghan economy at relatively high frequency and with partial information.
authors: Hany Abdel-Latif & Abdullah Alhassan & Karim Badr & Iyke Maduako
title: Nowcasting Economic Activity in Afghanistan
title_zh: 阿富汗经济活动即时预测

abstract: We provide the first quantitative general-equilibrium assessment of the trade and welfare effects of the India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), a proposed rail-to-sea trade route through the Arabian Peninsula. We translate changes in transit times and transportation cost into bilateral trade costs and use them to inform a structural gravity counterfactual for over 200 countries and territories. We estimate that the declines in trade costs from IMEC would be modest, averaging 3.6 percent among affected pairs. Our results indicate that IMEC would benefit the GCC countries and Jordan most, with these countries gaining from the enhanced overland connectivity and more direct access to trade partners in Europe, North America, and North Africa. Upper- and lower-bound scenarios highlight the nonlinear role of relative rail and sea freight rates and the value of time in determining the corridor’s effectiveness, while additional sensitivity exercises show that transit delays can substantially reduce route adoption and the resulting gains.
authors: Mitchell W. Boice & Mr. Ken Miyajima
title: Alternative Trade Corridors of the GCC: The Case of IMEC
title_zh: 海合会的替代贸易走廊：以IMEC为例

abstract: This paper introduces the Global Pension Reform Database (GPRD), the first dataset to provide systematic coverage of pension reforms across 142 advanced, emerging, and developing economies from 1952 to 2025. Leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) through a ring-fenced, locally hosted large language model (LLM), we extract and classify more than 4,000 pension reform episodes from the Economist Intelligence Unit and the U.S. Social Security Administration by type, timing, status, and generosity, enabling consistent cross-country and historical analysis. Stylized facts show that pension reform has shifted from an advanced-economy phenomenon to a global and recurring policy tool, often clustered around fiscal and macroeconomic crises. An empirical application demonstrates its analytical potential: in non-advanced economies, implemented pension reforms are associated with statistically significant and persistent declines in the public debt-to-GDP ratio, suggesting that such reforms can contribute to sustained fiscal consolidation.
title: Global Pension Reform Database 1952 – 2025: From Narrative to Data Using AI
title_zh: 全球养老金改革数据库1952–2025：从叙事到数据的AI应用

abstract: We examine if European firms face binding financial constraints that explain Europe’s persistent scale-up gap. Using corporate tax changes as exogenous shocks and a "debt test", we analyze 7 million predominantly private firms across 20 euro area countries (2000–2022). A higher corporate tax rate increases the value of interest deductibility and, absent frictions, induces firms to increase leverage. We find that firms generally increase leverage after tax hikes, indicating constraints are not broadly binding. However, young firms and those in innovation-intensive industries show weaker responses. Among innovative firms, constraints vary: young firms appear unconstrained, while small, mature ones face binding constraints. Our findings suggest that financing frictions in Europe are concentrated among specific firm types at particular development stages, indicating that they are important at the critical scale-up stage.
authors: Mr. Luis Brandão-Marques & Alexandra Fotiou & Lea Havemeister & Mr. Richard Varghese
title: Are European Firms Financially Constrained?
title_zh: 欧洲企业是否面临融资约束？

abstract: This paper develops a global DSGE model linking oil-dependent economies to the systemic economies, and applies it to the GCC countries. The model features a range of nominal and real rigidities, extensive macrofinancial linkages, and diverse spillover transmission channels. Its modular structure also encompasses common features of oil-dependent economies, including a state-owned oil company, a capital intensive oil extraction technology, a sovereign wealth fund, an oil consumption subsidy, and membership of an international oil cartel. The calibrated model is used to simulate global risk and domestic reform scenarios the GCC economies, revealing how their distinct structural characteristics shape their responses to shocks.
title: A Global DSGE Model for Oil-Dependent Economies
title_zh: 一个面向石油依赖型经济体的全球DSGE模型

abstract: Fiscal rules and fiscal councils are often adopted independently: many countries operate under fiscal rules without a fiscal council, while fiscal councils are frequently established only after a fiscal rule is already in place, suggesting that the two institutions may contribute differently to fiscal discipline. This paper starts with a simple theoretical framework to explain these stylized facts, accounting for the fact that governments, or even society at large, may not always be in favour of a fiscal council. The model also predicts that a sufficient strengthening of a budget balance rule, an independent fiscal council, and an increased interaction between rule strength and council strength all help reduce the expected deficit. The ensuing empirical analysis, using the updated 2025 IMF datasets on fiscal rules and fiscal councils, tests these predictions for a large country sample, including 32 advanced economies and 58 emerging market and developing economies spanning from 2000 to 2024. We find indicative evidence that, depending on the sample and the institutional design, both stronger rules and councils are associated with lower primary deficits, reduced projection biases and improved forecast accuracy. We also find some role for the interaction between the strengths of rules and councils, although the pattern varies.
authors: Mr. Roel M. W. J. Beetsma & Mr. Waikei Raphael Lam & Mr. Marcos Poplawski Ribeiro & Alexandra Solovyeva
title: On the Role and Effectiveness of Fiscal Rules and Independent Fiscal Councils
title_zh: 财政规则与独立财政委员会的作用及有效性

abstract: Asian and Pacific economies face mounting fiscal pressures from high and rising debt and interest rates and significant spending needs in light of successive shocks. In the coming years, these fiscal strains will likely be exacerbated by the fiscal implications of structural trends in demography, technology, geoeconomic fragmentation, and climate transitions. To address these mounting fiscal challenges, domestic revenue mobilization will be imperative. Based on a comparative analysis with global peers, this paper provides an integrated assessment of the opportunities for enhanced revenue mobilization across the region, drawing on newly compiled data and indicators for cross-country revenue, tax design and tax administration. It documents comparatively low tax-to-GDP ratios and sizable tax potential, alongside marked differences in policy design and administrative capacity across income groups. The paper identifies five areas for reform for Asian and Pacific countries: strengthening value-added taxation; rationalizing corporate income tax incentives; expanding recurrent property taxation; accelerating digitalization in tax administration; and building public trust in tax administration. The appropriate sequencing differs across countries, but durable domestic revenue mobilization requires policy and administration to be treated as an integrated system, embedded in medium-term revenue strategies, and adapted to structural transitions and institutional capacity.
authors: Ikuo Saito & Ms. Jimena Acedo & Mr. Ruud de Mooij & Chenghong Wang & Ross Warwick

title: Options for Tax System Reform in Asia and the Pacific

abstract: This paper estimates the macroeconomic impact from a sudden cutoff in a country’s access to frontier AI services, once that country has grown to rely on them as an input to its economy. Applied through the production network framework of Baqaee and Farhi (2019) and calibrated to a representative small open economy, the headline GDP loss is 0.2 percent. The range of possible outcomes can vary significantly, however, depending on the future convergence path of competitor models and on the substitutability of AI across sectors. In the most severe scenario, the economic impact reaches 0.41 percent of GDP.
title: The Macroeconomic Impact of AI Access Disruptions
